paragraphs: 4M investigates how a single vision model can support many tasks and kinds of information. Its training inputs and outputs span text, images, geometry, semantic information, and feature maps produced by neural networks. A unified Transformer encoder-decoder learns across these modalities through a masked modeling objective: it uses available information to predict information that has been hidden.

The central design choice is to convert all modalities into discrete tokens. This gives otherwise different kinds of data a shared representational format. Training operates on a small, randomly selected subset of tokens, providing a way to scale multimodal learning without processing every token at once.

The experiments show several forms of versatility. Trained models perform diverse vision tasks directly and adapt effectively through fine-tuning to new tasks or input modalities. They also generate outputs conditioned on different modalities, supporting flexible multimodal editing. These findings establish the potential of this training scheme for broadly capable vision models, while presenting it as a step toward that goal.
neurips-2023-4m-massively-multimodal-mas.tldr: 4M trains one Transformer across tokenized visual and textual modalities, enabling varied vision tasks, adaptation, and multimodal generation.

paragraphs: HEADLINES turns historical newspaper publishing practices into a source of examples of similar meaning. Local U.S. newspapers often reproduced stories supplied by newswires while writing their own headlines. Different headlines attached to the same underlying story therefore provide naturally occurring pairs of short texts that summarize closely related content.

Building the dataset requires finding those connections in newly digitized newspapers. The researchers use page layout and language understanding to associate headlines with articles. They then apply deep neural methods to identify articles derived from the same source, despite substantial noise and shortened versions. The associated headlines become positive semantic similarity pairs.

The publicly available dataset contains nearly 400 million such pairs, covering 1920 through 1989. Its contribution combines scale with historical breadth, extending beyond datasets built mainly from contemporary web text or smaller annotation efforts. It is intended to support contrastively trained similarity models and research into how meaning varies across places and periods. The abstract presents these as uses the dataset enables.
neurips-2023-a-massive-scale-semantic-si.tldr: HEADLINES uses independently written headlines for reproduced newspaper stories to build nearly 400 million historical semantic similarity pairs.

paragraphs: AdaPlanner addresses a weakness in language-model agents that carry out sequences of actions: a plan can become unsuitable as the environment responds. Choosing actions greedily or following a fixed plan becomes increasingly problematic as tasks grow more complex and extend over more steps. The proposed agent instead revises its own plan using feedback received during execution.

The system combines in-plan and out-of-plan refinement strategies, making adaptation part of its planning process. It also uses prompts written in a code-like structure to support plan generation and mitigate hallucination. A skill discovery mechanism reuses successful plans as examples, helping the agent plan and revise with fewer task demonstrations.

Experiments report improvements over state-of-the-art baselines of 3.73% in ALFWorld and 4.11% in MiniWoB++, while using respectively two times and 600 times fewer samples. These results support the value of combining feedback-driven revision with reusable successful examples in the evaluated environments. The contribution concerns both stronger sequential decision-making and reduced dependence on demonstrations.
neurips-2023-adaplanner-adaptive-plannin.tldr: AdaPlanner improves language-model agents by revising plans from environmental feedback and reusing successful plans as examples.

paragraphs: This paper revisits why adversarial training had not become a strong defense for graph neural networks against malicious changes to graph structure. The researchers identify both theoretical and practical limitations in the graph learning setting used by earlier work. Addressing those limitations is part of their proposed route to making adversarial training effective.

A second contribution concerns how the network passes information through the graph. The authors find that flexible networks with learnable graph diffusion can adjust to adversarial perturbations. Their learned message-passing behavior also admits a natural interpretation, connecting robustness to an adaptable and understandable way of using graph connections.

The paper additionally introduces an attack that targets several nodes simultaneously while respecting both graph-wide and node-specific constraints. This expands the structural attacks that can be handled within the investigation. Combining the revised learning setting, adaptable networks, and attack contribution, the authors demonstrate state-of-the-art defense against structural perturbations. The result shows that the earlier shortcomings of adversarial training in this area can be overcome through these changes.
neurips-2023-adversarial-training-for-gr.tldr: Revising the learning setting, using adaptable graph diffusion, and developing stronger structural attacks makes adversarial training a state-of-the-art graph defense.

paragraphs: A model's confidence can exceed its actual reliability. Calibration methods try to address this mismatch, often evaluating it by grouping predictions with similar probabilities. This paper introduces Partitioned Calibration Error, a broader definition that exposes the grouping of data as a central difference among existing calibration error measures.

The authors argue that an accurate model should be calibrated across any partition, motivating groups based on input meaning as well as predicted probabilities. Their analysis connects accuracy and calibration to how finely the data is divided. This makes the choice and granularity of groups substantive parts of the calibration problem.

To put the analysis into practice, the method jointly learns a grouping function from deep model features and logits. It then learns a separate calibration function for each resulting subset. Experiments across multiple datasets and network architectures show significant performance improvements. The findings support treating semantically meaningful grouping as a component to learn, rather than taking probability-based groups as the only available structure.
neurips-2023-beyond-probability-partitio.tldr: Learning semantically meaningful data groups and calibrating each separately improves calibration across the evaluated datasets and architectures.

paragraphs: ComSL tackles speech-to-text translation by combining publicly available models already trained separately on speech and language. Joint learning across these two forms of information is difficult because it demands substantial data and GPU resources, and because speech and text have different representations. The composite architecture starts from capabilities those existing models have already acquired.

The training approach combines transfer learning with cross-modality learning. It adapts the pretrained components to downstream tasks while simultaneously learning connections between speech and language through multiple tasks. This design makes the relationship between the two modalities part of adaptation itself, with the stated aim of using training data efficiently.

On the public CoVoST2 evaluation set, ComSL achieves a state-of-the-art average BLEU score of 31.5 for translating speech in 21 languages into English text. The reported result demonstrates the effectiveness of the combined architecture and learning approach for that multilingual translation setting. Its broader contribution is a way to assemble and adapt existing speech and language models for spoken-language tasks.
neurips-2023-comsl-a-composite-speech-la.tldr: ComSL jointly adapts pretrained speech and language models, achieving a 31.5 average BLEU score on 21-language speech-to-English translation.

paragraphs: DinoSR combines three ideas for learning speech representations without externally supplied supervision: masked modeling, self-distillation, and online clustering. The aim is to create useful internal descriptions of speech through training signals derived from the audio itself. The paper argues that these components complement one another within a single representation-learning system.

A teacher network first converts input audio into contextualized embeddings, so the representation of a sound reflects its surrounding audio. An online clustering process groups those embeddings into discrete units described as a machine-discovered inventory of speech sounds. These units then provide targets that guide a student network. The teacher's continuous representations are thus turned into discrete supervision for the student.

The authors report performance beyond previous state-of-the-art methods on several downstream tasks. They also analyze the model and the discrete units it learns, examining the representations behind those results. The findings support this combination of teacher-generated information, clustering, and masked learning as an effective approach to speech representation learning.
neurips-2023-dinosr-self-distillation-an.tldr: DinoSR turns a teacher network's audio representations into clustered speech units that supervise a student, improving several downstream tasks.

paragraphs: FACTS audits subgroup fairness by examining recourse: how people could obtain a desired model outcome. It uses counterfactual explanations to study the changes associated with reaching that outcome. The central concern is whether members of different subgroups face different difficulties, making access to a favorable decision part of the fairness assessment.

The paper revisits and generalizes existing fairness definitions and introduces more refined ones. These distinguish an individual perspective, which considers subgroup members separately, from a collective perspective, which considers the subgroup as a whole. The authors also seek definitions that remain robust to the cost assigned to recourse, with some notions potentially independent of that cost.

These definitions are paired with an explainable, configurable framework that can evaluate models without relying on a particular model architecture. Experiments on several benchmark datasets demonstrate its applicability, efficiency, and advantages. The contribution is both conceptual and practical: it expands the ways recourse disparities can be described and provides a framework for auditing them.
neurips-2023-fairness-aware-counterfactu.tldr: FACTS audits subgroup fairness through counterfactual explanations of how difficult it is for people to obtain desired outcomes.

paragraphs: A neural network can perfectly fit noisy training data and still predict well on new examples. Benign overfitting describes cases where such a predictor performs nearly optimally. Tempered overfitting describes useful but suboptimal performance that worsens with increasing noise. This paper investigates how these two behaviors can arise within nonlinear neural networks.

The authors study a simple classification setting using two-layer ReLU networks. Under various assumptions, they prove a transition from tempered overfitting for one-dimensional inputs to benign overfitting in high dimensions. The result gives input dimension a central role in determining what fitting noisy data means for prediction quality in this setting.

Experiments at intermediate dimensions support the importance of this dimensional transition. The work helps connect two seemingly different descriptions of neural-network generalization through a shared theoretical setting. Its conclusions are tied to the studied networks and assumptions, while also highlighting interactions among dimension, sample size, architecture, and training algorithm. Perfect training fit alone therefore does not describe the resulting overfitting behavior.
neurips-2023-from-tempered-to-benign-ove.tldr: For two-layer ReLU classifiers under studied assumptions, increasing input dimension shifts overfitting from useful but suboptimal to nearly optimal.

paragraphs: Solving a game requires determining its outcome under optimal play and may also require constructing a complete strategy. This creates a different demand from playing extremely well: a winning strategy must handle every possible opposing move, including very poor ones. Those unusual positions can be absent from the self-play experience used to train AlphaZero-based prediction models.

The paper studies adapting these models during the solving search itself. It proposes two online fine-tuning methods that learn heuristics tailored to game solving. The motivation is to improve evaluations of positions encountered during search, where predictions inherited from self-play can be highly inaccurate.

On a series of challenging 7-by-7 Killall-Go problems, online fine-tuning uses 23.54% of the computation time required by the baseline without it. The results suggest that savings grow with problem size. The authors also describe the approach as extendable to other tree-search algorithms for problem solving, making adaptation during search the broader methodological contribution.
neurips-2023-game-solving-with-online-fi.tldr: Fine-tuning prediction models during game-solving search substantially reduces computation on the evaluated 7-by-7 Killall-Go problems.

paragraphs: Contrastive learning commonly compares two examples through the dot product of their feature vectors. Although this can produce useful representations, individual features may lack clear meaning and change substantially with initialization. This paper studies how modifying that comparison can make the learned features more identifiable and easier to interpret.

Tri-factor contrastive learning inserts a learnable diagonal matrix between the two feature vectors. Each diagonal entry weights a corresponding feature, giving the method a way to learn feature importance alongside the representation. The authors show that this extension can obtain identifiable features and order them by their learned importance.

Highly weighted features capture shared properties within classes and show strong interpretability in the reported analysis. Using only a few features also produces superior image-retrieval performance in the evaluation. The objective can be incorporated into contrastive methods including SimCLR and CLIP. The contribution is a relatively small change to the comparison rule that addresses feature stability, interpretation, and usefulness together, with minimal reported overhead.
neurips-2023-identifiable-contrastive-le.tldr: TriCL learns a weight for each contrastive feature, yielding identifiable, importance-ordered representations with improved interpretability and compact image retrieval.

paragraphs: When an overparameterized regression model has multiple solutions that fit its training data perfectly, the optimization procedure influences which solution it reaches. This preference is its implicit bias. The paper studies that preference through a simplified linear network in which every weight matrix has rank one, proposed as a proxy for standard linear networks.

The authors identify a potential function whose minimum, subject to zero training error, characterizes the solution reached by gradient descent. They then analyze how stochastic gradient descent changes that potential through its added noise. This explicitly connects the selected solution to network depth, initialization, and the use of stochastic updates.

A further result identifies a bias produced jointly by stochasticity and overparameterization that can reduce dependence on initialization. The authors compare their conclusions with those from diagonal linear networks and find the rank-one model's behavior more consistent with standard linear networks. This supports its possible usefulness as a proxy, without claiming a complete characterization of ordinary linear networks.
neurips-2023-implicit-bias-of-stochastic.tldr: A rank-one linear-network analysis connects optimization's implicit bias to depth, initialization, and noise that can reduce initialization dependence.

paragraphs: This paper treats a language model as a computational layer that maps input text to a distribution over possible output texts. Its prompt becomes a parameter that can be optimized. Feeding one such layer's output into another creates a Deep Language Network, allowing the researchers to study prompt learning across a sequence of models.

The authors first develop prompt optimization for a single layer, then extend it to a two-layer network with two prompts to learn jointly. The intermediate text produced by the first model is treated as a latent variable requiring inference. Variational inference provides the framing for learning prompts while accounting for that intermediate output.

Experiments test the single-layer method on reasoning and language-understanding tasks and show that the two-layer version can achieve higher performance. The results suggest the possibility of approaching GPT-4 performance using individually smaller, less powerful models. That comparison is presented as a promising direction, while the demonstrated contribution is joint prompt optimization and gains from the tested two-layer composition.
neurips-2023-joint-prompt-optimization-o.tldr: Treating intermediate text as a latent variable enables joint prompt optimization across two language-model layers, which can outperform one layer.

paragraphs: Graph-level representation learning converts an entire graph into a vector usable for tasks such as classification. This paper develops a learning principle inspired by the Lovász number, a graph-theoretic quantity related to global graph characteristics and providing an upper bound on graph Shannon capacity. The goal is to bring that global structural information into learned representations.

The authors examine the handle vector used in computing the Lovász number and argue that it is potentially suitable as a graph representation. Directly using this vector is difficult and problematic, so they introduce a neural-network approach to address those obstacles. This produces their proposed Lovász principle.

An enhanced version also uses Lovász numbers of subgraphs directly and efficiently. Experiments report competitive performance against baselines in both unsupervised and semi-supervised graph-level learning. The findings support this mathematical quantity as a useful source of guidance for representation learning, with neural networks providing a practical route from the graph-theoretic motivation to vectors used in downstream tasks.
neurips-2023-lovasz-principle-for-unsupe.tldr: The Lovász principle uses graph-theoretic global structure to guide neural graph representations, achieving competitive unsupervised and semi-supervised results.

paragraphs: MEMTO detects unusual behavior in time series containing multiple interacting variables. These data are difficult because relationships occur both across time and between variables. Reconstruction-based models attempt to reproduce their inputs, but excessive generalization can weaken their ability to distinguish anomalies. The paper addresses this issue with a Transformer guided by a learned memory.

The memory module learns how strongly each stored item should be updated in response to incoming data. A two-phase training procedure uses K-means clustering to initialize those memory items and stabilize learning. For detection, MEMTO measures deviations in both the original input space and the model's internal representation space, combining two views of abnormality.

Across five real-world datasets from diverse domains, the method achieves an average anomaly-detection F1 score of 95.74%, significantly exceeding previous state-of-the-art methods in the reported evaluation. Additional experiments support the effectiveness of its main components. These findings connect the memory mechanism and dual-space detection criterion to stronger performance on the evaluated multivariate time series.
neurips-2023-memto-memory-guided-transfo.tldr: MEMTO combines adaptive memory with input-space and latent-space deviations to improve multivariate time-series anomaly detection.

paragraphs: Local differential privacy protects individual data before it reaches a collector, removing the need to trust that collector with raw records. This protection can reduce statistical usefulness. The paper studies that tradeoff through functional local differential privacy, which expresses privacy in terms of a hypothesis-testing problem and has connections to Gaussian distributions.

The analysis covers estimation of a one-dimensional mean and nonparametric density estimation. Using contraction properties of privacy mechanisms and information-theoretic arguments, the authors derive minimax lower bounds: limits on the best worst-case estimation performance permitted by the privacy constraint. They establish an interpretable, continuous relationship between privacy strength and statistical utility.

The authors also propose Gaussian local-privacy mechanisms that attain the corresponding minimax upper bounds. A numerical study finds them superior to counterparts derived under epsilon-local differential privacy. Together, the optimality results and numerical evidence motivate the authors' recommendation to consider Gaussian local privacy a reliable standard. The theoretical conclusions concern the estimation problems analyzed in the paper.
neurips-2023-minimax-risks-and-optimal-p.tldr: The paper derives optimal estimation guarantees under functional local privacy and proposes Gaussian mechanisms with a continuous privacy–utility tradeoff.

paragraphs: MVDoppler explores recognizing walking behavior through small movements measured by radar. Optical perception relies heavily on visible geometry, which becomes difficult to capture at long distances. Doppler measurements offer another source of information: the abstract describes their micro-motion resolution as substantially more resilient to distance than geometric features.

The paper introduces a large dataset with multiple radar views and baseline models for gait analysis and classification. It specifically captures the effects of walking trajectory and radar observation angle, factors that existing datasets had not adequately represented. Baseline methods combine multiple views to mitigate their influence on classification.

The reported demonstrations show that less than a second of micro-motion data can be sufficient to detect hand-movement patterns reliably and even changes in walking behavior associated with phone distraction. This is a sufficiency finding in the demonstrated setting, rather than a requirement for every observation. The dataset and accompanying methods make viewpoint and movement trajectory explicit parts of studying radar-based behavioral perception.
neurips-2023-mvdoppler-unleashing-the-po.tldr: MVDoppler provides multi-view radar data and models showing that brief micro-motion observations can reveal hand movements and phone-related gait changes.

paragraphs: Non-rigid registration aligns shapes that can bend or deform. Methods based on spatial proximity can fail when deformations are large, while methods using abstract high-dimensional embeddings can be sensitive to perturbed or unfamiliar inputs. This paper combines learned correspondences with explicit deformation to address weaknesses of both approaches without correspondence supervision.

The framework moves a source mesh toward a target point cloud using correspondences derived from deep functional maps. It updates those correspondences as registration progresses and filters them through a consistency prior. An additional orientation regressor, trained on separately generated aligned synthetic shapes, reduces the requirement that inputs already have matching spatial orientations.

With as few as dozens of training shapes of limited variability, the system achieves state-of-the-art results on several non-rigid point-cloud matching benchmarks. It also produces high-quality correspondences for challenging unseen pairs with substantial extrinsic and intrinsic deformations, where the compared traditional and intrinsic approaches fail. The findings support continually revising learned correspondences during deformation as a way to strengthen the overall registration process.
neurips-2023-non-rigid-shape-registratio.tldr: Combining mesh deformation with dynamically updated deep functional-map correspondences improves non-rigid shape matching without correspondence supervision.

paragraphs: KL divergence measures differences between probability distributions, but its direction matters. This paper studies how the two directions relate when both distributions are multivariate Gaussians. It derives an exact supremum for divergence in one direction when divergence in the reverse direction is bounded by a positive value.

For a small bound epsilon, that supremum is epsilon plus a leading correction of twice epsilon to the three-halves power, followed by higher-order terms. This quantifies approximate symmetry when Gaussian KL divergence is small. The paper also derives an infimum in the reverse direction when the original divergence exceeds a specified threshold and states when these extrema can be attained.

For three Gaussian distributions, the authors establish a relaxed triangle inequality that controls the divergence between the first and third through bounds involving the middle distribution. All the theorem bounds are independent of dimension. This makes the results relevant to reasoning about Gaussian distributions with many coordinates, and the paper discusses applications in deep learning, reinforcement learning, and sample complexity.
neurips-2023-on-the-properties-of-kullba.tldr: Dimension-independent bounds quantify approximate symmetry and a relaxed triangle inequality for KL divergence between multivariate Gaussians.

paragraphs: ProteinShake is a Python package for building datasets and evaluating deep-learning models that use protein structures. It supports both custom datasets and preprocessed collections drawn from the Protein Data Bank and AlphaFoldDB. Its purpose is to make structure data easier to access and model comparisons easier to carry out.

Datasets come with prediction tasks and evaluation functions spanning a broad range of biological challenges. This connects data preparation to concrete questions and shared ways of measuring model performance. The benchmark also examines different representations of protein structure, including graphs, voxel grids, and point clouds.

Three findings emerge from the reported benchmark. Pretraining almost always improves performance, the best representation depends on the task, and models have difficulty generalizing to new structures. These results make the benchmark useful for examining both effective modeling choices and transfer to unfamiliar inputs. In particular, the task dependence of representation quality means the evaluated biological problems do not share a single consistently optimal data modality.
neurips-2023-proteinshake-building-datas.tldr: ProteinShake simplifies protein-structure benchmarking and finds benefits from pretraining, task-dependent representation choices, and difficulty generalizing to new structures.

paragraphs: This paper investigates what self-supervised learning builds inside a network by inspecting its learned representations. The empirical study spans different models, architectures, and hyperparameters. Its focus is the internal organization that develops during training and how that organization relates to later classification performance.

The analysis finds that representations develop clusters associated with semantic labels, with the regularization component of the training objective driving this process. These clusters both improve downstream classification and compress information. The finding assigns regularization a substantive role in shaping useful semantic structure within the learned representation.

The authors also compare alignment with meaningful classes against alignment with random functions and find stronger alignment with the former. Semantic organization appears at multiple levels of a class hierarchy and becomes more pronounced deeper in the network. Together, these empirical observations explain how representations can become useful for different class sets. They connect the training objective, network depth, and semantic clustering to the behavior observed after self-supervised training.
neurips-2023-reverse-engineering-self-su.tldr: An empirical analysis finds that self-supervised regularization promotes semantic clustering, with stronger class alignment in deeper network representations.

paragraphs: SALT models time series whose dynamics change between discrete states. Existing autoregressive hidden Markov models support exact inference and straightforward parameter estimation, but capturing long histories requires many parameters and can cause overfitting. Switching linear dynamical systems represent long-range dependencies more compactly, yet their likelihood and parameter estimation are harder to handle.

The proposed model factorizes the parameter tensor of an autoregressive hidden Markov model into a low-rank form. This controls the number of parameters while supporting longer temporal dependencies. The construction aims to retain the useful inference properties of the autoregressive approach while gaining a more compact description of dynamics.

The paper proves theoretical connections and discusses practical relationships between SALT, linear dynamical systems, and switching linear dynamical systems. Experiments show quantitative advantages on simulated and real prediction problems, including behavioral and neural data. The learned low-rank tensor also reveals temporal dependencies within each discrete state, giving the model an interpretive role alongside its predictive one.
neurips-2023-switching-autoregressive-lo.tldr: SALT uses low-rank tensor factors to model changing time-series dynamics compactly while retaining useful autoregressive inference and interpretation.

paragraphs: The Harvard USPTO Patent Dataset organizes more than 4.5 million English-language patent applications filed between 2004 and 2018. It preserves inventor-submitted applications alongside structured metadata and all text fields. This gives researchers access to how an invention was described when first submitted, enabling analysis of patentability at filing time.

The dataset links language with structured information about each application. That combination supports studying how prediction changes across different contexts. As a demonstration, the authors introduce patent acceptance prediction and use the metadata to investigate concept shifts. Models trained in one context perform worse when evaluated across different innovation categories or time periods.

The paper also demonstrates subject-area classification, language modeling, and abstractive summarization. HUPD is two to three times larger than comparable corpora, but its contribution also rests on the filing-stage documents and accompanying metadata. Together, these features support research on language models in a large, changing domain where performance across categories and over time is an explicit concern.
neurips-2023-the-harvard-uspto-patent-da.tldr: HUPD provides over 4.5 million patent applications with metadata and shows that acceptance-prediction performance declines across categories and time.

paragraphs: Tree-Ring Watermarking places a fingerprint into a diffusion model's image-generation process. The watermark starts as a pattern in the initial noise vector and subtly influences sampling as a whole. The resulting fingerprint is described as invisible to people, allowing generated images to carry a detectable signal without an obvious visual mark.

The patterns are constructed in Fourier space to be invariant to transformations including convolutions, cropping, dilation, flipping, and rotation. Detection works by inverting the diffusion process to recover a noise vector and checking it for the embedded pattern. Generation and detection therefore operate through the noise representation underlying the image.

The authors demonstrate the method as a plug-in for diffusion models, including text-conditioned Stable Diffusion, with negligible loss in FID. They report substantially greater robustness than deployed watermarking alternatives. The contribution is a way to connect model-output identification with the generation process itself, using structured noise patterns to support detection after common image transformations.
neurips-2023-tree-rings-watermarks-invis.tldr: Tree-Ring Watermarking embeds invisible Fourier-structured patterns in diffusion noise and detects them by reversing the generation process.

paragraphs: An ensemble defense combines several classifiers trained to resist adversarial attacks. Although this strategy has worked empirically, the reasons for its robustness advantages have been less clear. This paper develops an error theory for ensemble adversarial defense, proving a reduction in classification error on challenging sample sets in the analyzed adversarial scenarios.

The theory motivates interactive global adversarial training, or iGAT. One component uses a probabilistic rule to distribute examples that are difficult for the ensemble among individual classifiers. Another adds regularization aimed at the classifiers' most severe weaknesses. These components make the training of each classifier responsive to difficulties faced by the group.

Tests apply iGAT to several existing ensemble-defense techniques on CIFAR10 and CIFAR100 under both white-box and black-box attacks. The reported performance gains reach up to 17%, rather than representing a uniform improvement across all evaluations. The paper connects a theoretical account of ensemble benefits with a practical way to coordinate adversarial training.
neurips-2023-understanding-and-improving.tldr: iGAT uses ensemble error theory to coordinate adversarial examples and address individual classifiers' weaknesses, yielding reported gains of up to 17%.
